name: TeamStarWolf - Web Application Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of ATT&CK techniques commonly encountered during web application, API, and application-security testing. This is not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: WEB_APPLICATION_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, WEB_APPLICATION_PENTESTING.md, API_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, SECURE_CODING_REFERENCE.md, PENETRATION_TESTING_METHODOLOGY.md, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl.
blurb: Web and API intrusion paths, including application exploitation, account abuse, session theft, and data access. A curated practitioner view based on the library's application-security references.

name: TeamStarWolf - CWE Weakness Classes
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE CWE-to-ATT&CK mapping. Selects CWE records whose abstraction is Class, follows their explicit related_capec links, then the linked CAPEC records' explicit attack_techniques values. Only live (non-revoked) techniques in data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl are included; a CAPEC link to an id ATT&CK v19 revoked is shown under its successor (data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl). These indirect associations support exploration, not a claim that a weakness always produces the technique. Sources: CWE_REFERENCE.md, CAPEC_REFERENCE.md, data/weaknesses/cwe.jsonl, data/weaknesses/capec.jsonl, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. No hierarchy inheritance is inferred. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Connects CWE weakness classes to ATT&CK behaviors through explicit CAPEC links in the library. These indirect associations support investigation; they do not mean a weakness always produces the behavior.

name: TeamStarWolf - CAPEC Families
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Families are represented by non-deprecated CAPEC Meta-abstraction patterns with explicit attack_techniques values in data/weaknesses/capec.jsonl. Includes only IDs present in data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Sources: CAPEC_REFERENCE.md and those two data files. Meta patterns with no explicit mapping are omitted; child-pattern mappings and inherited relationships are not inferred. This is a partial family view, not the complete CAPEC catalog. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Shows techniques explicitly linked to broad CAPEC Meta patterns in the library. This partial family view excludes patterns without direct mappings and does not infer child-pattern relationships.

name: TeamStarWolf - Cloud Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of cloud intrusion behaviors, not an official MITRE mapping. Selects explicit technique references from CLOUD_ATTACK_REFERENCE.md for account abuse, administrative execution, credential access, discovery, data theft, persistence, and impact. Technique IDs and displayed tactics come from data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. This is a selected overview, not an exhaustive cloud matrix. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Covers selected cloud intrusion behaviors, from account and token abuse to data theft and destructive impact. A curated overview drawn from the library's cloud attack reference.

name: TeamStarWolf - Active Directory
description: Curated practitioner view of Active Directory intrusion behaviors, not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: ACTIVE_DIRECTORY_ATTACK_REFERENCE.md, ACTIVE_DIRECTORY_ATTACKS.md, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Selects explicitly referenced techniques for enumeration, credential access, Kerberos and NTLM abuse, certificate abuse, remote execution, and persistence. Tactics are taken from the technique profiles, not inferred from document section labels. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Covers domain reconnaissance, credential theft, Kerberos and NTLM abuse, certificate attacks, and remote access. A curated view drawn from the library's Active Directory references.

name: TeamStarWolf - Ransomware TTPs
description: Curated practitioner view of ransomware intrusion and extortion behaviors, not an official MITRE mapping and not an attribution to any particular group. Sources: the ATT&CK intrusion-chain table in RANSOMWARE_DEFENSE_REFERENCE.md and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Includes the reference's explicit initial access, execution, credential access, lateral movement, defense impairment, collection, exfiltration, and impact techniques. Scores indicate membership only, not frequency in incidents.
blurb: Follows common ransomware intrusion themes through access, credential theft, movement, exfiltration, encryption, and recovery inhibition. A curated view of behaviors, without attribution to a particular group or claims about incident frequency.

name: TeamStarWolf - SolarWinds and SUNBURST 2019-2021
description: Techniques in the SolarWinds and SUNBURST intrusion (2019 to 2021), not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: the ATT&CK SolarWinds Compromise campaign (C0024) and software S0559, S0560, S0562, S0565 as published in ATT&CK v20, plus techniques mapped only by the Mandiant, CrowdStrike, Microsoft and CISA reports. Tactics are taken from data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Scores indicate membership only. Each comment names source numbers from the Sources table of case-studies/SOLARWINDS_SUNBURST.md.
blurb: Techniques from the SolarWinds and SUNBURST record, from the SUNSPOT build implant and the signed Orion backdoor to the Cobalt Strike loaders and the Golden SAML cloud follow-on. A curated layer for the SolarWinds case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - Container and Kubernetes Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of container and Kubernetes attack behaviors, not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: the ATT&CK Containers Matrix table in CONTAINER_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, the shell-execution detection example in KUBERNETES_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Selects only explicit technique references from those sources; this is not exhaustive Kubernetes coverage. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Covers container deployment, image abuse, host escape, workload discovery, and unauthorized compute use. A curated selection from the container and Kubernetes references, with limited coverage.

name: TeamStarWolf - OWASP Top 10 (2021)
description: Curated practitioner view of the OWASP Top 10 (2021) themes used in SECURE_CODING_REFERENCE.md, not an official OWASP or MITRE mapping. The 2021 edition is intentional and is not a claim to represent the latest Top 10. Sources: that reference's A01-A10 sections and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Associations describe possible attacker behavior or defensive context, not equivalence between a weakness category and an ATT&CK technique. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Connects the library's OWASP Top 10 (2021) themes with relevant attacker behaviors. These curated associations are not an official OWASP or MITRE crosswalk.

name: TeamStarWolf - Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified Log4Shell record supports: ATT&CK procedures and campaigns C0017 and C0018, CISA advisories AA22-174A and AA22-320A, Cisco Talos, CrowdStrike, Check Point, and ATT&CK v20.0 STIX relationships citing the CrowdStrike and Check Point Log4j reports. Ids reported under earlier ATT&CK versions are shown under their v20.0 successors from data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/LOG4SHELL.md. Scores: 100 ties the technique to Log4j exploitation itself, 75 is post-exploitation behavior in a Log4j-initiated intrusion, 40 is an Inferred mapping no opened source cites.
blurb: Techniques from the Log4Shell record, from exploitation and scanning to the post-exploitation behavior of APT41, Aquatic Panda, Magic Hound and AvosLocker intrusions. A curated layer for the Log4Shell case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - npm Supply-Chain Attacks, 2018 to 2026
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques that the verified npm supply-chain record supports: ATT&CK v20.0 procedures and software mappings for S9008 Shai-Hulud, S9043 Mini Shai-Hulud, S9042 CanisterWorm, S9041 TeamPCP Cloud Stealer, S9034 Tsundere Botnet, S1246 BeaverTail, G1056 TeamPCP, G0082 APT38 and G1052 Contagious Interview, and the maintainer, vendor and GitHub reports the study cites. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/NPM_SUPPLY_CHAIN_ATTACKS.md. Scores: 100 is an ATT&CK-published link to an npm worm, loader or group in the record, 50 is the study's own mapping, labelled Inferred.
blurb: Techniques from eight years of npm supply-chain attacks, from hijacked maintainer accounts and poisoned release workflows to install-time payloads, token theft and exfiltration to code repositories. A curated layer for the npm supply-chain case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - Hugging Face AI Supply Chain (Enterprise)
description: Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the Hugging Face case study. Score 100: an ATLAS-published ATT&CK reference on a technique ATLAS maps in a Hugging Face case study, or an ATT&CK procedure that names Hugging Face (S9035). Score 50: the study's own inference, labelled Inferred in its comment. Comments carry the study's source numbers.
blurb: The Enterprise techniques behind the Hugging Face case study: malicious models, loader exploits, exposed tokens and the July 2026 pipeline intrusion. Score 100 marks a MITRE-published link, 50 the study's labelled inference.

name: TeamStarWolf - ICS attacks 2024 to 2026 (Enterprise)
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK Enterprise techniques that the verified record of the ICS 2024 to 2026 case study supports: CISA advisories AA23-335A, AA24-038A, AA25-343A and AA26-097A, and ATT&CK v20.0 pages C0041, C0063, G1017 and S9046 (C0063 rows from data/attack/campaign_profiles.jsonl). Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/ICS_ATTACKS_AND_ADVISORIES_2024_2026.md. Score 100 means membership only.
blurb: The IT-side techniques behind 2024 to 2026 ICS incidents: default accounts on exposed PLCs, edge-appliance exploitation and credential theft, the Poland wiper intrusion chain and the IOControl implant. A curated layer for the ICS 2024 to 2026 case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - Stuxnet (S0603) Enterprise
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise techniques that ATT&CK v20.0 lists for Stuxnet (S0603), each with a comment naming source numbers from case-studies/STUXNET.md; every row cites the Symantec W32.Stuxnet Dossier v1.4. Each selected technique is shown under all its tactics. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: The Windows side of Stuxnet: USB and network spread, privilege escalation, signed rootkit drivers and Step 7 project infection. A curated layer for the Stuxnet case study; the ICS techniques are in a separate ics-attack layer.

name: TeamStarWolf - APT41 Public Record
description: Curated view of the techniques bound in the TeamStarWolf case study APT41: The Public Record, 2012 to 2026 (case-studies/APT41_PUBLIC_RECORD.md). Not an official MITRE mapping. Score 100: ATT&CK v20.0 records the technique for G0096 APT41 or its attributed campaigns C0017 and C0040. Score 60: a vendor or government primary states the id in its own ATT&CK table (revoked ids normalized through data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl). Score 30: the study's own inference from a dated report. Each comment names the study's source numbers. Campaign C0012 Operation CuckooBees is left out because ATT&CK attributes it to no group.
blurb: Techniques from the public APT41 record, 2012 to 2026: what ATT&CK records for G0096 and campaigns C0017 and C0040, what vendor and government primaries state, and the study's own labelled inferences. A curated layer for the APT41 case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - Change Healthcare Attack 2024
description: Techniques in the Change Healthcare ransomware attack of February 2024, not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: Andrew Witty's House and Senate testimony and UHG's answers for the record, the State of Nebraska complaint, FBI, CISA and HHS advisory AA23-353A, and ATT&CK software S1068 BlackCat as published in ATT&CK v20. Tactics are taken from data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Scores: 100 is documented in the Change record, 75 is alleged in the Nebraska complaint, 40 is ALPHV/BlackCat general tradecraft not documented at Change. Each comment names source numbers from the Sources table of case-studies/CHANGE_HEALTHCARE_2024.md.
blurb: Techniques from the Change Healthcare record, from the single-factor Citrix login to the February 2024 encryption, with ALPHV/BlackCat general tradecraft shown separately. A curated layer for the Change Healthcare case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - Ghostcat CVE-2020-1938 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat) record supports: the Apache Tomcat advisory, Chaitin's and CNVD's disclosures, the 2020 scanning reports, the CISA KEV listing, and the TeamStarWolf lab run of 3 November 2026 on Tomcat 9.0.30 against a 9.0.31 control. No CTID mapping exists for this CVE, so every row is the study's own mapping. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/GHOSTCAT_CVE_2020_1938.md. Scores: 100 is demonstrated in the lab, 75 is reported in the public record, 40 is a defender-side check or a follow-on stage the lab did not run.
blurb: Techniques from the Ghostcat record, from the unauthenticated AJP file read the lab demonstrated to the scanning and the follow-on stages it did not run. A curated layer for the Ghostcat CVE-2020-1938 case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - ProFTPD mod_copy (CVE-2015-3306) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the ProFTPD mod_copy (CVE-2015-3306) case study. No opened source names an ATT&CK technique for this CVE, so every binding is the study's own mapping, labelled in its comment. Scores: 100 is behavior the lab run of 4 November 2026 demonstrated, 75 is a documented exploitation path the lab did not demonstrate, 40 is actor context from joint advisory AA26-281A not tied to a ProFTPD intrusion. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/PROFTPD_MOD_COPY_CVE_2015_3306.md.
blurb: Techniques from the ProFTPD mod_copy record: the unauthenticated file copy the lab demonstrated, the web-shell path it did not, and the scanning AA26-281A describes. A curated layer for the CVE-2015-3306 case study.

name: TeamStarWolf - The Year 2020 in Intrusions Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified 2020 intrusion record supports: CISA, FBI, NSA and NCSC advisories of 2020 (AA20-099A to AA20-352A), vendor reports, regulator findings and Red Canary's 2020 telemetry. Ids printed under earlier ATT&CK versions are shown under their v20.0 successors from data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl. Scores: 100 the source prints the id, 75 the source describes the behavior and the mapping is the study's, 50 only a press account supports it, 40 an Inferred mapping.
blurb: Techniques from the 2020 record: edge-device exploitation, password spraying, the SolarWinds supply chain, and the Ryuk, Maze and WastedLocker ransomware intrusions. A curated layer for the 2020 chronicle case study; the ICS techniques from AA20-205A are in a separate ics-attack layer.

name: TeamStarWolf - Exchange Server Mass Exploitation 2021 (Operation Exchange Marauder) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified record of the 2021 Exchange Server mass exploitation supports: ProxyLogon and HAFNIUM-era intrusions (Microsoft, Volexity, Mandiant, Rapid7, ATT&CK G0125), follow-on actors on the same bugs (ESET, Microsoft, Talos, Red Canary, ATT&CK G0131), and the ProxyShell era (CISA AA21-321A and later ATT&CK group rows). Ids reported under earlier ATT&CK versions are shown under their v20.0 successors from data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/EXCHANGE_MARAUDER_2021.md. Scores: 100 ties the technique to ProxyLogon exploitation or HAFNIUM-era intrusions, 75 is follow-on actors on the same bugs or the ProxyShell era, 40 is an Inferred or demonstration-only mapping.
blurb: Techniques from the 2021 Exchange Server mass exploitation, from the ProxyLogon chain and HAFNIUM's mailbox theft to the ransomware, miners and ProxyShell actors that followed. A curated layer for the Exchange Marauder case study.
